title: Loaders
summary: Read data at the route boundary and keep requests out of rendering components.

sections.title: Define the read once
sections.body: A loader receives the URL, decoded path params, and a cancellation signal. Return the data the view needs. clientLoader runs in the browser; a server loader runs on the server when connected through the Vite integration or serverRoute. A plain manually registered function executes in the environment where that router runs.

sections.title: Register and render the route
sections.body: Manual registration associates a URL pattern with the module. File routing derives /tasks/:id from tasks.$id/route.ts. Export the handler and view from that module. The tasks service above is application code: its read method returns a typed task or an Error.

sections.title: Consume the inferred result
sections.body: typeof connects the hook to the handler return type without importing that handler at runtime. File proximity alone does not supply a generic type to TypeScript. Passing a typed route definition to useLoaderData is the alternative that infers the result from an argument.

sections.title: Query strings belong to request.url
sections.body: params contains path captures, not search fields. Use URLSearchParams for filters and sorting. A GET Form navigates to the query URL and triggers this loader. Keep the filter in the returned data if the view needs to render the active value.

sections.title: Initial loading and later revalidation
sections.body: Routes renders HydrateFallback while the initial data is unavailable. A successful undefined result still counts as loaded. Later revalidation can keep the current view visible with its existing data. shouldRevalidate controls subsequent reads; it cannot eliminate the first necessary load.

sections.title: Server loader with a client wrapper
sections.body: Keep loader and clientLoader as separate named exports. During SSR the server loader supplies the HTML data. Later browser loads use clientLoader, which may call serverLoader. A hydrated loaded snapshot avoids an automatic duplicate initial read. A client-only route with no server data loads in the browser.

sections.title: Load without navigating
sections.body: fetcher.load("/tasks/42") invokes the registered task loader but puts its result in fetcher.data. It does not replace the active page useLoaderData result or change the URL. This is useful for previews, dependent selects, and independent search. Reads do not trigger page revalidation.

sections.title: Cancellation and parallel requests
sections.body: Pass the provided signal into each network request. A newer navigation aborts the previous navigation request and prevents stale results from winning. Independent fetchers have their own cancellation channels. Use Promise.all for independent reads within a loader, and handle returned Error values before rendering the combined data.

sections.title: JSON across the server boundary
sections.body: Server transport and hydration serialize data. Prefer plain records, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. Dates become strings; functions and class instances do not retain their runtime behavior. A TypeScript return annotation cannot make a value survive serialization unchanged.
